Close all current connections? Apps reconnect on their own, and new connections will use the latest node.

Created: %1$s Subscriptions: %2$d
The app settings and override settings will be replaced, and the subscriptions of the backup are added. Subscriptions are downloaded again, which needs network.
Not restored (update them by hand on the profiles page): %1$s
Override and service settings take effect after reloading the profile or restarting the service.
Underlying = connections the core really has open to the node (far fewer than requests when multiplexing works). Requests = connections carried by the node.
All of this data already exists: failures from the core log, node speed-test results and the app\'s crash records. Connection failures start counting again when the core restarts.
No app crashes recorded. The proxy is not running, so connection failures and node timeouts cannot be shown.
Proxy is not running: connection failures and node timeouts are only available while it runs.
Nodes whose speed test timed out (%1$d)
Killed by the system for low memory
%1$s · last speed test timed out (no response, the node may be dead or blocked)
Timed out: the node did not answer in time; it may be dead, blocked, or the network is down
Connection refused: the port is closed or a firewall refused it
Connection reset: cut off by the peer or the network in between
The peer closed the connection early
Name resolution failed: the domain does not exist or DNS is unavailable
Network unreachable: no usable network or route
TLS / certificate error: invalid certificate, wrong system time or interference
Authentication failed: wrong account, password or key for the node
Rejected by a rule or the node
The server refused this ECH config; it may be out of date or not match the server

Tap ECH test to really connect once and check whether the fields written in the config work. Supported now: ech-opts of nodes. Certificates are not verified, only whether the handshake gets through. “Check DNS” asks every DNS server of the profile about the same domain (only dns: and hosts: are read).
Testing… each node waits a few seconds at most
Enter a domain that is certainly blocked and hosted by the node\'s server (or the CDN in front of it)
No node with ech-opts in the config, nothing to test. (Nodes of the final config after overrides count.)
OK, accepted by the server (%1$d ms)
Result: ECH works and the block is got around (connects with ECH, blocked without)
Result: ECH works, but it also connects without ECH, so this network does not block the domain and bypassing cannot be shown
Result: ECH does not work, the server refused the config (out of date or not matching the server)
Result: ECH does not work: it connects without ECH but not with it; bad config or unsupported server
Result: cannot tell, none of the %1$d addresses tried got through (network may be out, node down, server not hosting the domain; or it connected but the server did not accept ECH)
ECH config: the config written in the file
ECH config: fetched from DNS (HTTPS record of %1$s)
ech-opts is written but enable is not true, ECH is off
This node type (QUIC based, e.g. hysteria, tuic) does not use this TLS handshake, the test does not apply
Could not get the ECH config (HTTPS record of %1$s): %2$s

Note: "works" only means the server accepted this ECH config, not that the whole node path works. Nodes with the same ECH config are tested once; the test uses Go\'s own TLS and does not verify certificates.
This network has no IPv6: dialling an IPv6 address failed %1$d times (latest %2$s)
This speed test is older than the last network change, so the result may be out of date. Tap refresh, or test again on the proxy page.
This network has no IPv6: %1$d IPv6-only node(s) timed out in the speed test, which is expected and not counted as a timeout: %2$s
Enter a domain to look up (any domain, e.g. the blocked one you use above)
Apps get: the hosts entry %1$s → %2$s; DNS servers are not asked for this domain
Apps get: a fake-ip from the pool %1$s (the real address is looked up when the connection is made). Judged from the profile
Apps get: the real address (enhanced-mode is not fake-ip). Judged from the profile
Apps get: the real address, the domain is covered by the fake-ip-filter entry %1$s. Judged from the profile
Apps get: the real address (fake-ip-filter-mode is whitelist and no entry covers the domain). Judged from the profile
Cannot tell from the profile: fake-ip-filter has entries that cannot be judged here (e.g. %1$s)
Cannot tell from the profile: fake-ip-filter-mode is rule, each entry carries its own fake-ip / real-ip
Real answer of the core\'s own DNS server (dns.listen %1$s): fake-ip %2$s
Real answer of the core\'s own DNS server (dns.listen %1$s): real address %2$s
dns.listen is %1$s, but the core\'s DNS server gave no answer (not listening there, or nothing to answer)
The dns: section lists no DNS server (the core then uses its built-in defaults).
DNS servers in the profile (%1$d), each asked directly for A and AAAA:
answers (%1$d ms): NXDOMAIN, the domain does not exist
These addresses lie in the fake-ip pool: this server points back at the core itself
This type of server (%1$s) cannot be checked here
The core reaches this server through “%1$s”; it was asked directly here, so the result may differ
Written with h3=true; asked over HTTP/2 here
hosts maps %1$s to the name %2$s, so everything below is about %2$s
For an IPv6 question (AAAA) the answer is empty: fake-ip is on but no fake-ip-range6 is set
For an IPv6 question (AAAA) apps get a fake address from fake-ip-range6
For an IPv6 question (AAAA) the answer is empty: dns.ipv6 is false
use-hosts is false: the DNS server ignores the hosts: section
respect-rules is true: the core\'s own DNS queries follow the rules, a server reached through a proxy may behave differently from the direct test below

Note: only the dns: and hosts: sections are read. Every server is asked directly; the “Core resolver” line is the answer of the core itself and shows what it really takes from them (it may come from the core’s DNS cache; use “Clear cache” first for a fresh one). A DoH server that answers something other than a DNS message (JSON, a web page) shows what it sent in the reason.
the address cannot belong to a real site (private, reserved or Teredo range)
it says NXDOMAIN while other servers resolve the name
its addresses share no network with what the encrypted servers answered
Verdict: every server that answered says NXDOMAIN. The name most likely does not exist, this is not a DNS fault.
The name may be mistyped, did you mean %1$s ?
The name has no dot, it looks like only a part of a domain was entered.
Verdict: %1$d server(s) gave answers that are very likely forged (DNS pollution / hijacking):
Verdict: %1$d server(s) disagree with the encrypted DNS servers. A CDN that hands out other addresses by region does that too, so this is only a suspicion:
Addresses from the encrypted servers (DoH / DoT, they cannot be rewritten on the way): %1$s
Verdict: the servers agree, no sign of pollution.
Verdict: only one server gave addresses, there is nothing to compare with.
Core resolver: not available (no profile is loaded).
Core resolver answers (%1$d ms): NXDOMAIN, the domain does not exist
Core resolver, what it really answers (%1$d ms; after its nameserver / fallback / policy choice, without hosts and fake-ip):\n A: %2$s; AAAA: %3$s
It matches none of the servers below (the core\u2019s DNS cache, or it took another result).
nameserver-policy: the pattern %1$s covers this domain, so the core asks %2$s (not nameserver)
nameserver-policy: none of its %1$d entries covers this domain, so nameserver / fallback answer
These entries cannot be judged here and might cover it: %1$s
These entries come first and cannot be judged here, one of them may cover the domain before that: %1$s
DNS cache and fake-ip map (also closes every connection)
The core’s DNS cache was cleared. The next lookup asks the servers again.
The DNS cache and the fake-ip map were cleared and every connection was closed. Apps that kept an old fake address connect again with a new lookup.
Clearing failed (the core has no resolver loaded).
Go back to an earlier version of an edited profile, see what changed, or check a config for errors
There is no imported profile yet.
Only profiles you edit yourself (not subscriptions) keep a history. A subscription is downloaded again on every save.
No earlier version is kept yet. A version is kept each time you save an edited profile.
Compare with the version in use
Removes %1$d line(s) of the version in use, adds %2$d line(s):
This version is identical to the one in use.
Restore the version of %1$s? The version in use stays in the history, so you can go back. Edits you have not saved are dropped.
Restored and saved. If the profile is in use, the core loads it again.
Not restored, the config in use stays as it is: %1$s
No error found. The core can parse this config.
(This is the edit you have not saved yet.)
One zip with the config (secrets masked), recent errors, node connections, crash records and a DNS check

The zip holds the active config (passwords, ids and keys replaced by ***), recent errors and connection failures, the node connection summary, crash records and a DNS check of the domain last typed on the config check page. It still contains node server addresses and the domains of recent failed connections: look through it before you send it to anyone.
%1$d files were written. Look through it before you send it to anyone.
%1$d fields the core added as defaults are hidden, tap here to show them
%1$d fields the core added as defaults are shown, tap here to hide them
No difference: the core runs what you wrote.
This is the saved config in use, laid out again in block style (comments are not kept); only the steps the core and the app do on loading are compared.
(anchor definition: unknown to the core, only used through references, not a difference)
▸ Blocks the core added by itself (%1$d), tap to open
▾ Blocks the core added by itself (%1$d), tap to close
None of them was changed by a later step. To see all the defaults, tap the line at the top.
Log level is now “%1$s”, in effect at once
Saved: log level “%1$s”, it counts when the profile is loaded again
Could not save the log level
Result: OK. The answer the core really uses matches %1$d server(s).
Result: not sure. The core\'s answer matches none of the checked servers; it may come from the core\'s DNS cache.
The core\'s answer: A %1$s; AAAA %2$s (%3$d ms)
Result: some answers are very likely fake (DNS pollution / hijacking), see the lines marked ⚠ below.
Result: some servers answer differently from the encrypted DNS and may be polluted (a CDN giving different addresses by region does that too), see the lines marked ⚠ below.
Result: no server gave an answer.
⚠ %1$d of the DNS servers the core really asks give a doubtful answer; this affects resolving directly, see below.

%1$d server(s) that only serve a special purpose answer differently from the encrypted DNS and may be polluted. They are not the main DNS (nameserver); they are only used for direct domains or for resolving the DoH servers themselves.
DNS the core really asks (nameserver, fallback, nameserver-policy)
DNS for a special purpose only (direct domains, DoH addresses, node domains)

In the Jianguoyun web page open Account info → Security → Third-party apps → Add app, and use the generated password below (not your login password). Use the same three values on every device that shares the backup. The backup is encrypted with the backup password before it is uploaded; if you forget it the backup cannot be opened. The values are kept on this device only.

%1$d subscriptions, the app settings and the override settings were encrypted and uploaded (%2$d KB, as \"%3$s\"). The access-control app list of this device is not part of it. This device keeps its newest 5 backups.
There is no backup on Jianguoyun yet. Back up from a device first.
The backup password is wrong, or the file is damaged. Check the backup password in the Jianguoyun settings (it must be the one used when the backup was made).
That file is not an encrypted backup of this app.

Backup of %1$s from %2$s (%3$d subscriptions).

The subscriptions of the backup are added to this device. Nothing is deleted; with the same name and address the one on this device stays (a file subscription is replaced by the backup's copy). Subscriptions are downloaded again, which needs network.

This device is saved first; "Undo last cloud restore" in the menu goes back.
Subscriptions on this device that are not in the backup will be DELETED: %1$s
If this is not what you wanted, use \"Undo last cloud restore\" in the menu.
Go back to this device as it was at %1$s, before the last cloud restore?
Also replace the settings of this device (app settings, service settings such as IPv6, override settings)
The settings of this device were not changed.
Delete the backup of %1$s from %2$s from Jianguoyun? It is removed for good and no device can restore it afterwards.
Already on this device (this device\'s stays): %1$s
File subscriptions replaced by the backup\'s content: %1$s
